newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares edge up, seen flat amid long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares edge up, seen flat amid long weekend.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse edged up in thin turnover and analysts expected another stable session on Friday, after the bourse is closed on Thursday for Corpus Christi holiday, as many investors take a long weekend.

The main market's WIG index rose 50.9 points, or 0.3 percent, to 15,802.6, and turnover fell 11.2 percent to 105.3 million zlotys ($32.9 million) on all three markets as 44 issues rose, 37 fell and 22 were flat.

Analysts said it was likely to maintain its almost 2.5-month sideways drift as forthcoming polls due in September and busy primary market were keeping some investors sidelined while no major selling was likely at current prices.
"The problem is people don't want to sell at current prices and others don't want to buy believing it will still be falling," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at PBI brokerage.
Analysts said that if the zloty stabilised after a two-percent fall since Thursday triggered by the Czech crown slump the bourse might moderately rise within the flat trend.
The stocks traded at average 15.5 times historic earnings.
Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday the main wave of foreign investor withdrawal from zloty instruments was likely to have ended.

But analysts said strong gains were unlikely as Poland's largest commercial Bank Handlowy SA offering of one-billion -zlotys worth of shares and copper giant KGHM offer seen in July were drawing capital from the bourse.
But they said said Handlowy's and KGHM's bourse entry seen in mid-year could help the bourse attract new capital in longer-term by boosting the exchange's capitalisation and liquidity.
